embeds.title: 🟡 Russian Hackers Turn Kazuar Backdoor Into Modular P2P Botnet
embeds.description:
**Actor:** Secret Blizzard
Microsoft researchers analyzed a recent variant of the Kazuar backdoor developed by the Russian hacker group Secret Blizzard, which has transformed the malware into a modular peer-to-peer botnet with three distinct modules (kernel, bridge, and worker) designed for long-term persistence, stealth, and data collection. The malware supports 150 configuration options and includes security bypasses for AMSI, ETW, and WLDP. Secret Blizzard, associated with the FSB and overlapping with Turla, Uroburos, and Venomous Bear, targets government, diplomatic, defense, and critical infrastructure organizations across Europe, Asia, and Ukraine.
**Sources:** BleepingComputer • 🔴 1 corroborating
**CVEs:** none • **Access:** n/a
**Incident date:** unknown • **Confidence:** reported
